Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed to review whether Australian law adequately protects the human right to religious freedom.

***

The appointment was announced by cabinet as the government seeks to avoid a divisive debate over religious amendments to a same-sex marriage bill. Treasurer Scott Morrison said the review should not replace consideration of those amendments.

***

Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull said the issue needed careful examination following the yes vote on marriage equality and the move toward related legislation.

***

Senior conservatives are divided on timing: some, including Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann, have suggested a religious freedom bill could be considered separately next year, while Morrison and senator David Fawcett want it addressed alongside the marriage bill.

***

Ruddock has been asked to report by 31 March. Turnbull said any broader reforms must be handled cautiously to avoid unintended consequences, and argued Ruddock was well suited to lead the review because of his human rights experience.
